227\. Revise newly redesignated §§ 1800.100 and 1800.101 to read as follows:

[§ 1800.100](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-1800.100)

Purpose.

This part adopts the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regulation in subparts A through F and applicable appendices of [2 CFR part 200](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200), as supplemented by this part, as the NASA policies and procedures for uniform administrative requirements, cost principles, and audit requirements for Federal awards. This part gives regulatory effect to the OMB regulation for Federal awards issued by NASA as supplemented by this part. See [2 CFR 200.110(a)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.110#p-200.110(a)) regarding the process for amending [2 CFR part 200](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200).

[§ 1800.101](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-1800.101)

Applicability.

(a) This part establishes policies and procedures for grants and cooperative agreements awarded by NASA to non-Federal entities, for-profit organization, foreign organizations, and foreign public entities as allowed by [2 CFR 200.101](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.101). For supplemental regulation, NASA has adopted section numbers that correspond to those in the OMB regulation in [2 CFR part 200](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200).

(1) Non-Federal entities must follow the policies and procedures appearing in subparts A through F and applicable appendices of [2 CFR part 200](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200) and as supplemented by this part.

(2) Foreign organizations and foreign public entities must follow the policies and procedures appearing in subparts A through E and applicable appendices of [2 CFR part 200](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200) and as supplemented by this part.

(3) U.S. and foreign for-profit organizations must follow the policies and procedures appearing in subparts A through D and applicable appendices of [2 CFR part 200](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200) and as supplemented by this part. The Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) at [48 CFR parts 30](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/part-30) and [31](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/part-31), takes precedence over the cost principles in [2 CFR part 200, subpart E](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200/subpart-E), [f](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200/subpart-f) or Federal awards to U.S. and foreign for-profit organizations.

(b) Throughout this part, the term “award” refers to both “grant” and “cooperative agreement” unless otherwise indicated.

(c)(1) In general, research with foreign organizations and foreign public entities will not be conducted through grants or cooperative agreements, but instead will be accomplished on a no-exchange-of-funds basis. In these cases, NASA enters into agreements undertaking projects of international scientific collaboration. NASA's policy on performing research with foreign organizations and foreign public entities on a no-exchange-of-funds basis is set forth at NASA FAR Supplement (NFS) at [48 CFR 1835.016-70](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-1835.016-70) and [1835.016-72](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-1835.016-72). In rare instances, NASA may enter into an international agreement under which funds will be transferred to a foreign recipient.

(2) Grants or cooperative agreements awarded to foreign organizations and foreign public entities are made on an


( printed page 32282)

exceptional basis only. Awards require the prior approval of the Headquarters Office of International and Interagency Relations and the Headquarters Office of the General Counsel. Requests to issue awards to foreign organizations are to be coordinated through the Office of Procurement, Procurement and Grants Policy Division.

L. 103-355, 108 Stat. 3327 ( [31 U.S.C. 6101 note](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/31/6101)); [42 U.S.C. 2473(c)(1)](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/42/2473); [E.O. 12549](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12549), [51 FR 6370](https://www.federalregister.gov/citation/51-FR-6370), [3 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-3), 1986 Comp., p. 189; [E.O. 12689](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12689), [54 FR 34131](https://www.federalregister.gov/citation/54-FR-34131), [3 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-3), 1989 Comp., p. 235.

[§ 1880.10](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-1880.10)

What does this part do?

This part adopts the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by this part, as the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) policies and procedures for nonprocurement debarment and suspension. This part gives regulatory effect to the OMB regulation for Federal awards issued by NASA, as supplemented by this part. This part satisfies the requirements in section 3 of [Executive Order 12549](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12549), “Debarment and Suspension” ( [3 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-3), 1986 Comp., p. 189), [Executive Order 12689](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12689), “Debarment and Suspension” ( [3 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-3), 1989 Comp., p. 235), and [31 U.S.C. 6101 note](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/31/6101) (section 2455, Pub. L. 103-355, 108 Stat. 3327).

[§ 1880.20](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-1880.20)

Does this part apply to me?

This part and, through this part, pertinent portions of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) (see table 2 to [2 CFR 180.100(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.100#p-180.100(b))) apply to you if you are a—

(a) Participant or principal in a “covered transaction” (see subpart B of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) and the definition of “nonprocurement transaction” at [2 CFR 180.970](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.970));

(b) Respondent in a NASA suspension or debarment action;

(c) NASA debarment or suspension official; or

(d) NASA grants officer, agreements officer, or other official authorized to enter into any type of nonprocurement transaction that is a covered transaction.

[§ 1880.30](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-1880.30)

What policies and procedures must I follow?

The NASA policies and procedures that you must follow are the policies and procedures specified in each applicable section of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as that section is supplemented by the section in this part with the same section number. The contracts that are covered transactions, for example, are specified by [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220) as supplemented by § 1880.220. For any section of OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) that has no corresponding section in this part, NASA policies and procedures are those in the OMB regulation.

# Subpart A—General

[§ 1880.137](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-1880.137)

Who in NASA may grant an exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction?

The Chief Acquisition Officer has the authority to grant an exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction, as provided in the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.135](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.135).

# Subpart B—Covered Transactions

[§ 1880.220](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-1880.220)

What contracts and subcontracts, in addition to those listed in [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220), are covered transactions?

NASA extends coverage of nonprocurement suspension and debarment requirements beyond first-tier procurement contracts under a covered nonprocurement action, to all lower tier subcontracts, at all dollar values, consistent with OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.220(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220#p-180.220(c)) and the figure in the appendix at [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180). NASA does not permit subcontracting to suspended or debarred entities at any tier, at any dollar amount.

# Subpart C—Responsibilities of Participants Regarding Transactions

[§ 1880.332](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-1880.332)

What methods must I use to pass requirements down to participants at lower tiers with whom I intend to do business?

You as a participant must include a term or condition in lower-tier transactions requiring lower-tier participants to comply with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by this subpart.

# Subpart D—Responsibilities of Federal Agency Officials Regarding Transactions

[§ 1880.437](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-1880.437)

What method do I use to communicate to a participant the requirements described in the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435)?

To communicate to a participant the requirements described in [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435), you must include a term or condition in the transaction that requires the participant's compliance with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by subpart C of this part, and requires the participant to include a similar term or condition in lower-tier covered transactions.

# Subparts E-J \[Reserved\]

# Subpart A—General

[§ 2000.10](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2000.10)

What does this part do?

This part promulgates a regulation adopting the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), establishing the United States Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) policies and procedures for nonprocurement debarment and suspension. NRC thereby gives regulatory effect to the OMB regulation. It also supplements the OMB regulation by identifying NRC implementing officials and identifying how to pass these requirements through to other entities.

[§ 2000.20](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2000.20)

Does this part apply to me?

This part and, through this part, pertinent portions of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) (see table 2 to [2 CFR 180.100(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.100#p-180.100(b))) apply to:

(a) Participant or principal in a “covered transaction”;

(b) Respondent in an NRC nonprocurement suspension or debarment action;

(c) NRC debarment or suspension official; or

(d) NRC grants officer, agreements officer, or other official authorized to enter into a covered nonprocurement transaction.

[§ 2000.30](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2000.30)

What policies and procedures must I follow?

(a) The NRC policies and procedures that you must follow are the policies and procedures specified in each applicable section of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), and those in this part. The NRC has closely tracked OMB's numbering scheme. For example, the contracts under a nonprocurement transaction that are covered transactions that are in [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220) are supplemented by § 2000.220.

(b) For any section of OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) that has no corresponding section in this part, NRC requirements are those in the OMB regulation at [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180).

[§ 2000.135](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2000.135)

Who in the Nuclear Regulatory Commission may grant an exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction?

The Director, Office of Administration or another official designated by the Director, has the authority to grant a written exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction, as provided in regulation at [2 CFR 180.135](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.135). The Director or other official designated by the Director shall explain the reason(s) for deviating from the Governmentwide policy.

# Subpart B—Covered Transactions

[§ 2000.220](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2000.220)

What contracts and subcontracts, in addition to those listed in [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220), are covered transactions?

The NRC nonprocurement suspension and debarment requirements apply only to first-tier procurement contracts under a covered nonprocurement transaction.

# Subpart C—Responsibilities of Participants Regarding Transactions

[§ 2000.330](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2000.330)

What method must be used to pass requirements down to participants at lower tiers?

A participant in a covered transaction must include a term or condition in any lower-tier covered transaction to require the participant of that transaction to—

(a) Comply with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180); and

(b) Include a similar term or condition in any covered transaction into which it enters at the next lower tier.

# Subparts D through H \[Reserved\]

# Subpart I—Definitions

[§ 2000.930](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2000.930)

Debarring official.

The debarring official for the United States Nuclear Regulatory Commission is the Director, Office of Administration.

[§ 2000.1010](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2000.1010)

Suspending official.

The suspending official for the United States Nuclear Regulatory Commission is the Director, Office of Administration.

[§ 2200.20](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2200.20)

Does this part apply to me?

This part and, through this part, pertinent portions of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) (see table 2 to [2 CFR 180.100(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.100#p-180.100(b))) apply to you if you are a—

(a) Participant or principal in a “covered transaction” (see subpart B of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) and the definition of “nonprocurement transaction” at [2 CFR 180.970](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.970));

(b) Respondent in a Corporation for National and Community Service suspension or debarment action;

(c) Corporation for National and Community Service debarment or suspension official; or

(d) Corporation for National and Community Service grants officer, agreements officer, or other official authorized to enter into any type of nonprocurement transaction that is a covered transaction.

[§ 2200.30](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2200.30)

What policies and procedures must I follow?

The Corporation for National and Community Service policies and procedures that you must follow are the policies and procedures specified in each applicable section of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as that section is supplemented by the section in this part with the same section number. The contracts that are covered transactions, for example, are specified by [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220) as supplemented by § 2200.220. For any section of OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) that has no corresponding section in this part, Corporation for National and Community Service policies and procedures are those in the OMB regulation.

[§ 2200.137](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2200.137)

Who in the Corporation for National and Community Service may grant an exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction?

The Chief Executive Officer (or another official designated by the Chief Executive Officer) has the authority to grant an exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction, as provided in the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.135](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.135).

[§ 2200.220](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2200.220)

What contracts and subcontracts, in addition to those listed in [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220), are covered transactions?

Although the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.220(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220#p-180.220(c)) allows a Federal agency to do so (also see optional lower tier coverage in the figure in appendix A to 2 CFR part 180), Corporation for National and Community Service does not extend coverage of nonprocurement suspension and debarment requirements beyond first-tier procurement contracts under a covered nonprocurement transaction.

[§ 2200.332](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2200.332)

What methods must I use to pass requirements down to participants at lower tiers with whom I intend to do business?

You as a participant must include a term or condition in lower-tier transactions requiring lower-tier participants to comply with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180).

[§ 2200.437](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2200.437)

What method do I use to communicate to a participant the requirements described in the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435)?

To communicate to a participant the requirements described in [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435), you as an agency official must include a term or condition in the transaction that requires the participant's compliance with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), and requires the participant to include a similar term or condition in lower-tier covered transactions.

( printed page 32285)


[§ 2245.10](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2245.10)

What does this part do?

This part requires that the award and administration of the Corporation for National and Community Service's (Corporation) grants and cooperative agreements comply with Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regulation implementing the portion of the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988 ( [41 U.S.C. 701-707](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/41/701), as amended, hereinafter referred to as “the Act”) that applies to grants. This part—

(a) Gives regulatory effect to the OMB regulation (subparts A through F of [2 CFR part 182](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-182)) for the Corporation's grants and cooperative agreements; and

(b) Establishes the Corporation's policies and procedures for compliance with the Act that are the same as those of other Federal agencies, in conformance with the requirement in [41 U.S.C. 705](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/41/705) for Government-wide implementing regulations.

[§ 2245.20](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2245.20)

Does this part apply to me?

This part and, through this part, pertinent portions of the OMB regulation in subparts A through F of [2 CFR part 182](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-182) (see [2 CFR 182.115(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-182.115#p-182.115(b))) apply to you if you are a—

(a) Recipient of a Corporation grant or cooperative agreement; or

(b) A Corporation awarding official.

[§ 2245.30](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2245.30)

What policies and procedures must I follow?

(a)
_General._
You must follow the policies and procedures specified in applicable sections of the OMB regulation in subparts A through F of [2 CFR part 182](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-182), as implemented by this part.


(b)
_Specific sections of OMB regulation that this part supplements._
In implementing the OMB regulation in [2 CFR part 182](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-182), this part supplements four sections of the OMB regulation, as shown in the following table. For each of those sections, you must follow the policies and procedures in the OMB regulation, as supplemented by this part.


| Section of OMB <br> regulation | Section in this part where<br> supplemented | What the supplementation clarifies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (1) [2 CFR 182.225(a)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-182.225#p-182.225(a)) | § 2245.225 | Whom in the Corporation a recipient other than an individual must notify if an employee is convicted for a violation of a criminal drug statute in the workplace. |
| (2) [2 CFR 182.300(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-182.300#p-182.300(b)) | § 2245.300 | Whom in the Corporation a recipient who is an individual must notify if he or she is convicted of a criminal drug offense resulting from a violation occurring during the conduct of any award activity. |
| (3) [2 CFR 182.500](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-182.500) | § 2245.500 | Who in the Corporation is authorized to determine that a recipient other than an individual is in violation of the requirements of [2 CFR part 182](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-182), as implemented by this part. |
| (4) [2 CFR 182.505](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-182.505) | § 2245.505 | Who in the Corporation is authorized to determine that a recipient who is an individual is in violation of the requirements of [2 CFR part 182](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-182), as implemented by this part. |

(c)
_Sections of the OMB regulation that this part does not supplement._
For any section of OMB regulation in subparts A through F of [2 CFR part 182](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-182) that is not listed in paragraph (b) of this section, the Corporation's policies and procedures are the same as those in the OMB regulation.


240\. Revise § 2245.400 to read as follows:

[§ 2245.400](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2245.400)

L. 100-690, Title V, Subtitle D; [41 U.S.C. 701-707](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/41/701)).

[§ 2336.10](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2336.10)

What does this part do?

This part adopts the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by this part, as the Social Security Administration (SSA) policies and


( printed page 32286)

procedures for nonprocurement debarment and suspension. L. 103-355, 108 Stat. 3327).


[§ 2336.20](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2336.20)

Does this part apply to me?

This part and, through this part, pertinent portions of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) (see table 2 to [2 CFR 180.100(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.100#p-180.100(b))) apply to you if you are a—

(a) Participant or principal in a “covered transaction” (see subpart B of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) and the definition of “nonprocurement transaction” at [2 CFR 180.970](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.970));

(b) Respondent in an SSA suspension or debarment action;

(c) SSA debarment or suspension official; or

(d) SSA grants officer, agreements officer, or other official authorized to enter into any type of nonprocurement transaction that is a covered transaction.

[§ 2336.30](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2336.30)

What policies and procedures must I follow?

The SSA policies and procedures that you must follow are the policies and procedures specified in each applicable section of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by the section in this part with the same section number. The contracts that are covered transactions, for example, are specified by [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220), as supplemented by § 2336.220. For any section of OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) that has no corresponding section in this part, SSA policies and procedures are those in the OMB regulation.

# Subpart A—General

[§ 2336.137](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2336.137)

Who in the SSA may grant an exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction?

(a) Within the Social Security Administration, the Commissioner or the designated agency debarment official may grant an exception permitting an excluded person to participate in a particular covered transaction. If the Commissioner or the designated agency debarment official grants an exception, the exception must be in writing and state the reason(s) for deviating from the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.135](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.135).

(b) An exception granted by one agency for an excluded person does not extend to the covered transactions of another agency.

# Subpart B—Covered Transactions

[§ 2336.220](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2336.220)

What contracts and subcontracts, in addition to those listed in [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220), are covered transactions?

Although the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.220(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220#p-180.220(c)) allows a Federal agency to do so (also see option lower tier coverage in the figure in appendix A to 2 CFR part 180), SSA does not extend coverage of nonprocurement suspension and debarment requirements beyond first-tier procurement contracts under a covered nonprocurement transaction.

# Subpart C—Responsibilities of Participants Regarding Transactions

[§ 2336.332](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2336.332)

What methods must I use to pass requirements down to participants at lower tiers with whom I intend to do business?

You as a participant must include a term or condition in lower-tier transactions requiring lower-tier participants to comply with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by this subpart.

# Subpart D—Responsibilities of Federal Agency Officials Regarding Transactions

[§ 2336.437](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2336.437)

What method do I use to communicate to a participant the requirements described in the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435)?

To communicate to a participant the requirements described in [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435), you must include a term or condition in the transaction that requires the participant's compliance with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by subpart C of this part, and requires the participant to include a similar term or condition in lower-tier covered transactions.

245\. Revise §  2339.400 to read as follows:

[§ 2339.400](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2339.400)

What method do I use as an agency awarding official to obtain a recipient's agreement to comply with the OMB regulation?

You must include the following term or condition in the award:

_Drug-free workplace._

L. 100-690, Title V, Subtitle D; [41 U.S.C. 701-707](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/41/701)).

247\. The authority citation for part 2424 continues to read as follows:

L. 103-355, 108 Stat. 3327; [E.O. 12549](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12549), [3 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-3), 1986 Comp., p. 189; [E.O. 12689](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12689), [3 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-3), 1989 Comp., p. 235.

248\. Revise § 2424.10 to read as follows:

[§ 2424.10](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2424.10)

What does this part do?

In this part, the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) implements, as HUD policies, procedures, and requirements for nonprocurement debarment and suspension, the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by this part. This adoption thereby gives regulatory effect for HUD to the OMB regulation for Federal awards issued by HUD, as supplemented by this part. This part satisfies the requirements in section 3 of [Executive Order 12549](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12549), “Debarment and Suspension” ( [3 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-3), 1986 Comp., p. 189), [Executive Order 12689](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12689), “Debarment and Suspension” ( [3 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-3), 1989 Comp., p. 235), and [31 U.S.C. 6101 note](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/31/6101) (section 2455, Pub. L. 103-355, 108 Stat. 3327).

249\. Revise § 2424.30 to read as follows:

[§ 2424.30](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2424.30)

What policies and procedures must I follow?

The HUD policies and procedures that you must follow are the policies and procedures specified in each applicable section of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as that section is supplemented by the section in this part with the same section number. The contracts that are covered transactions, for example, are specified by [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220), as supplemented by § 2424.220. For any section of OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) that has no corresponding section in this part, HUD policies and procedures are those in the OMB regulation.

250\. Revise § 2424.220 to read as follows:

[§ 2424.220](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2424.220)

What contracts and subcontracts, in addition to those listed in [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220), are covered transactions?

In addition to the contracts covered under [2 CFR 180.220(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220#p-180.220(b)), this part applies to any contract, regardless of tier, that is awarded by a contractor, subcontractor, supplier, consultant, or its agent or representative in any transaction, if the contract is to be funded or provided by HUD under a covered nonprocurement transaction and the amount of the contract is expected to equal or exceed $25,000. This extends the coverage of the HUD nonprocurement suspension and debarment requirements to all lower tiers of subcontracts under covered nonprocurement transactions, as permitted under the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.220(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220#p-180.220(c)) (see optional lower-tier coverage in the figure in appendix A to 2 CFR part 180).

251\. Revise § 2424.332 to read as follows:

[§ 2424.332](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2424.332)

What methods must I use to pass requirements down to participants at lower tiers with whom I intend to do business?

To communicate the requirements to lower-tier participants, you must include a term or condition in the transaction requiring compliance with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by this subpart.

252\. Revise § 2424.437 to read as follows:

[§ 2424.437](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2424.437)

What method do I use to communicate to a participant the requirements described in the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435)?

To communicate to a participant the requirements described in [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435), you must include a term or condition in the transaction that requires the participant to: comply with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by subpart C of this part, and include a similar term or condition in lower-tier covered transactions.

# PART 2429—REQUIREMENTS FOR DRUG-FREE WORKPLACE (FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE)

253\. The authority citation for part 2429 continues to read as follows:

( printed page 32288)
Authority:[41 U.S.C. 701-707](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/41/701); [42 U.S.C. 3535(d)](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/42/3535).

254\. Revise §§ 2429.10 through 2429.30 to read as follows:

[§ 2429.10](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2429.10)

What does this part do?

This part requires that the award and administration of Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) grants and cooperative agreements comply with Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regulation implementing the portion of the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988 ( [41 U.S.C. 701-707](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/41/701)) (referred to as the Act in this part) that applies to grants. This part:

(a) Gives regulatory effect to the OMB regulation (subparts A through F of [2 CFR part 182](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-182)) for HUD grants and cooperative agreements; and

(b) Establishes HUD policies and procedures for compliance with the Act that are the same as those of other Federal agencies, in conformance with the requirement in [41 U.S.C. 705](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/41/705) for Governmentwide implementing regulations.

[§ 2429.20](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2429.20)

Does this part apply to me?

This part, and through this part, pertinent portions of the OMB regulation in subparts A through F of [2 CFR part 182](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-182) (see [2 CFR 182.115(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-182.115#p-182.115(b))) apply to you if you are a:

(a) Recipient of a HUD grant or cooperative agreement; or

(b) HUD awarding official.

[§ 2429.30](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2429.30)

What policies and procedures must I follow?

(a)
_General._
You must follow the policies and procedures specified in applicable sections of the OMB regulation in subparts A through F of [2 CFR part 182](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-182), as implemented by this part.


(b)
_Specific sections of OMB regulation that this part supplements._
In implementing the OMB regulation in [2 CFR part 182](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-182), this part supplements four sections of the OMB regulation, as shown in the following table. For each of those sections, you must follow the policies and procedures of the OMB regulation, as supplemented by this part.


| Section of OMB<br> regulation | Section in this<br> part where <br> supplemented | What the supplementation clarifies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (1) [2 CFR 182.225(a)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-182.225#p-182.225(a)) | § 2429.225 | Whom in HUD must a recipient other than an individual notify if an employee is convicted for a violation of a criminal drug statute in the workplace? |
| (2) [2 CFR 182.300(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-182.300#p-182.300(b)) | § 2429.300 | Whom in HUD must a recipient who is an individual notify if he or she is convicted of a criminal drug offense resulting from a violation occurring during the conduct of any award activity? |
| (3) [2 CFR 182.500](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-182.500) | § 2429.500 | Who in HUD is authorized to determine that a recipient other than an individual is in violation of the requirements of [2 CFR part 182](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-182), as implemented by this part? |
| (4) [2 CFR 182.505](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-182.505) | § 2429.505 | Who in HUD is authorized to determine that a recipient who is an individual is in violation of the requirements of [2 CFR part 182](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-182), as implemented by this part? |

(c)
_Sections of the OMB regulation that this part does not supplement._
For any section of OMB regulation in subparts A through F of [2 CFR part 182](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-182) that is not listed in paragraph (b) of this section, HUD policies and procedures are the same as those in the OMB regulation.


255\. Revise § 2429.400 to read as follows:

[§ 2500.10](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2500.10)

Adoption of [2 CFR part 200](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200).

(a) Under the authority cited for this part, the National Science Foundation (NSF) has formally adopted [2 CFR part 200](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200). This part adopts the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regulation for Federal awards issued by the NSF. See [2 CFR 200.110(a)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.110#p-200.110(a)) regarding the process for amending [2 CFR part 200](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200).The Foundation's implementation document, the NSF Proposal & Award Policies & Procedures Guide, may be found at:
_[www.nsf.gov/​publications/​pub\_​summ.jsp?​ods\_​key=​papp](http://www.nsf.gov/publications/pub_summ.jsp?ods_key=papp)._

(b) NSF's implementation includes the following deviation from the Uniform Grants Regulation:

(1)
_Award Cash Management System._
NSF is continuing collection of award financial information through the implementation of the Award Cash Management Service (ACM$) and the Program Income Worksheet. ACM$ replaced the NSF Federal Financial Report (FFR) and the NSF FastLane Cash Request process with a single web-based user interface. ACM$ is used to collect award level detail financial information at the time of each payment request submitted by the awardee institution. The Program Income Worksheet is used to collect program income financial information from awardee institutions on an annual basis. ACM$ and the Program Income Worksheet utilize approved Government-wide data elements from the FFR for the collection of financial information as prescribed in [2 CFR 200.328](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.328). The requirement for Federal agencies to use the FFR data elements for cash management and financial reporting was publicly announced in
**Federal Register**
on August 13, 2008.

[§ 2520.10](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2520.10)

What does this part do?

This part adopts the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by this part, as the National Science Foundation (NSF) policies and procedures for nonprocurement debarment and suspension. This part gives regulatory effect for NSF to the OMB regulation as supplemented by this part. This part satisfies the requirements in section 3 of [Executive Order 12549](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12549), “Debarment and Suspension” ( [3 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-3), 1986 Comp., p. 189), [Executive Order 12689](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12689), “Debarment and Suspension” ( [3 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-3), 1989 Comp., p. 235), and [31 U.S.C. 6101 note](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/31/6101) (section 2455, Pub. L. 103-355, 108 Stat. 3327).

[§ 2520.20](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2520.20)

Does this part apply to me?

This part and, through this part, pertinent portions of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) (see table 2 to [2 CFR 180.100(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.100#p-180.100(b))) apply to you if you are a—

(a) Participant or principal in a “covered transaction” (see subpart B of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) and the definition of “nonprocurement transaction” at [2 CFR 180.970](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.970)).

(b) Respondent in an NSF suspension or debarment action.

(c) NSF debarment or suspension official.

(d) NSF grants officer, agreements officer, or other official authorized to enter into any type of nonprocurement transaction that is a covered transaction.

[§ 2520.30](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2520.30)

What policies and procedures must I follow?

The NSF policies and procedures that you must follow are the policies and procedures specified in each applicable section of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as that section is supplemented by the section in this part with the same section number. The contracts that are covered transactions, for example, are specified by [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220) as supplemented by § 2520.220. For any section of OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) that has no corresponding section in this part, NSF policies and procedures are those in the OMB regulation.

# Subpart A—General

[§ 2520.137](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2520.137)

Who in NSF may grant an exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction?

The NSF Director and the Deputy Director have the authority to grant an exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction.

# Subpart B—Covered Transactions

[§ 2520.220](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2520.220)

What contracts and subcontracts, in addition to those listed in [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220), are covered transactions?

Although the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.220(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220#p-180.220(c)) allows a Federal agency to do so (also see optional lower tier coverage in the figure in appendix A to 2 CFR part 180), NSF does not extend coverage of nonprocurement suspension and debarment requirements beyond first-tier procurement contracts under a covered nonprocurement transaction.

# Subpart C—Responsibilities of Participants Regarding Transactions

[§ 2520.332](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2520.332)

What methods must I use to pass requirements down to participants at lower tiers with whom I intend to do business?

You as a participant must include a term or condition in lower-tier transactions requiring lower-tier participants to comply with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by this subpart.

# Subpart D—Responsibilities of Federal Agency Officials Regarding Transactions

[§ 2520.437](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2520.437)

What method do I use to communicate to a participant the requirements described in the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435)?

To communicate to a participant the requirements described in [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435), you must include a term or condition in the transaction that requires the participant's compliance with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by subpart C of this part, and requires the participant to include a similar term or condition in lower-tier covered transactions.

As approved by the Archivist of the United States, the National Archives does not permit grant recipients to use allocated funds from NARA or NHPRC for indirect costs. Grant recipients may use cost sharing to cover indirect costs instead. NARA's policies on indirect costs are located at
_[www.archives.gov/​nhprc](http://www.archives.gov/nhprc),_
and are included in grant opportunity announcements.


[§ 2600.102](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2600.102)

Additional NARA grant administration policies.

Grant recipients must also follow NARA grant administration policies and procedures set out in [36 CFR parts 1202](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1202), [1206](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1206), [1208](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1208), [1211](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1211), and [1212](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1212).

260\. Revise §§ 2700.10 through 2700.30 to read as follows:

[§ 2700.10](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2700.10)

What does this part do?

This part adopts the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by this part, as the Small Business Administration (SBA) policies and procedures for nonprocurement debarment and suspension. This part gives regulatory effect for SBA to the OMB regulation as supplemented by this part. This part satisfies the requirements in section 3 of [Executive Order 12549](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12549), “Debarment and Suspension” ( [3 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-3), 1986 Comp., p. 189); [Executive Order 12689](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12689), “Debarment and Suspension” ( [3 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-3), 1989 Comp., p. 235); and section 2455 of the Federal Acquisition Streamlining Act of 1994, Public Law 103-355 ( [31 U.S.C. 6101 note](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/31/6101)).

[§ 2700.20](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2700.20)

Does this part apply to me?

This part and, through this part, pertinent portions of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) (see table 2 to [2 CFR 180.100(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.100#p-180.100(b))) apply to you if you are a—

(a) Participant or principal in a “covered transaction” (see subpart B of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) and the definition of “nonprocurement transaction” at [2 CFR 180.970](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.970));

(b) Respondent in an SBA suspension or debarment action;

(c) SBA debarment or suspension official; or

(d) SBA grants officer, agreements officer, or other official authorized to enter into any type of nonprocurement transaction that is a covered transaction.

[§ 2700.30](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2700.30)

What policies and procedures must I follow?

The SBA policies and procedures you must follow are the policies and procedures specified in each applicable section of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as that section is supplemented by the section in this part with the same section number. The contracts that are covered transactions, for example, are specified by [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220) as supplemented by § 2700.220. For any section of OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) that has no corresponding section in this part, SBA policies and procedures are those in the OMB regulation.

261\. Revise subparts B through D to read as follows:

# Subpart B—Covered Transactions

[§ 2700.220](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2700.220)

What contracts and subcontracts, in addition to those listed in [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220), are covered transactions?

In addition to the contracts covered under [2 CFR 180.22(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.22#p-180.22(b)), this part applies to any contract, regardless of tier, that is awarded by a contractor, subcontractor, supplier, consultant, or its agent or representative in any transaction, if the contract is to be funded or provided by the SBA under a covered nonprocurement transaction and the amount of the contract is expected to equal or exceed $25,000. This extends the coverage of the SBA nonprocurement suspension and debarment requirements to all lower tiers of subcontracts under covered nonprocurement transactions, as permitted under the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.200(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.200#p-180.200(c)) (see optional lower tier coverage in the figure in appendix A to 2 CFR part 180).

# Subpart C—Responsibilities of Participants Regarding Transactions

[§ 2700.332](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2700.332)

What methods must I use to pass requirements down to participants at lower tiers with whom I intend to do business?

You, as a participant, must include a term or condition in lower-tier transactions requiring lower-tier participants to comply with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by this part.

# Subpart D—Responsibilities of Federal Agency Officials Regarding Transactions

[§ 2700.437](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2700.437)

What method do I use to communicate to a participant the requirements described in the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435)?

To communicate to a participant the requirements described in [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435), you must include a term or condition in the transaction that requires the participant's compliance with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by subpart C of this part, and requires the participant to include a similar term or condition in lower-tier covered transactions.

[§ 2867.10](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2867.10)

What does this part do?

L. 103-355, 108 Stat. 3327).

[§ 2867.20](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2867.20)

To whom does this part apply?

This part and, through this part, pertinent portions of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) (see table 2 to [2 CFR 180.100(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.100#p-180.100(b))) apply to any—

(a) Participant or principal in a “covered transaction” (sees subpart B of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) and the definition of “nonprocurement transaction” at [2 CFR 180.970](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.970) (as supplemented by subpart B of this part));

(b) Respondent in a Department of Justice suspension or debarment action;

(c) Department of Justice debarment or suspension official; or

(d) Department of Justice grants officer, agreements officer, or other official authorized to enter into any type of nonprocurement transaction that is a covered transaction.

[§ 2867.30](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2867.30)

What policies and procedures must be followed?

The Department of Justice policies and procedures that must be followed are the policies and procedures specified in each applicable section of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as that section is supplemented by the section in this part with the same section number. The contracts that are covered transactions, for example, are specified by [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220) as supplemented by § 2867.220. For any section of OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) that has no corresponding section in this part, Department of Justice policies and procedures are those in the OMB regulation.

# Subpart A—General

[§ 2867.137](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2867.137)

Who in the Department of Justice may grant an exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction?

Within the Department of Justice, the Attorney General or designee has the authority to grant an exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction, as provided in the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.135](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.135).

# Subpart B—Covered Transactions

[§ 2867.220](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2867.220)

What contracts and subcontracts, in addition to those listed in [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220), are covered transactions?

Although the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.220(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220#p-180.220(c)) allows a Federal agency to do so (also see optional lower tier coverage in the figure in appendix A to 2 CFR part 180), the Department of Justice does not extend coverage of nonprocurement suspension and debarment requirements beyond first-tier procurement contracts under a covered nonprocurement transaction.

# Subpart C—Responsibilities of Participants Regarding Transactions

[§ 2867.332](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2867.332)

What method must a participant use to pass requirements down to participants at lower tiers with whom the participant intends to do business?

A participant must include a term or condition in lower-tier transactions requiring lower-tier participants to comply with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by this subpart.

# Subpart D—Responsibilities of Federal Agency Officials Regarding Transactions

[§ 2867.437](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2867.437)

What method must be used to communicate to a participant the requirements described in the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435)?

To communicate to a participant the requirements described in [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435), the communication must include a term or condition in the transaction that requires the participant's compliance with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by subpart C of this part, and requires the participant to include a similar term or condition in lower-tier covered transactions.

# CHAPTER XXIX—DEPARTMENT OF LABOR

# PART 2900—UNIFORM ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENTS, COST PRINCIPLES, AND AUDIT REQUIREMENTS FOR FEDERAL AWARDS

269\. The authority citation for part 2900 continues to read as follows:

Authority:[5 U.S.C. 301](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/5/301); [2 CFR 200](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200).

270\. Revise §  2900.3 to read as follows:

[§ 2900.3](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2900.3)

Questioned cost.

In the Department of Labor, in addition to the regulation contained in [2 CFR 200.1](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.1), a questioned cost means a cost that is questioned by an auditor, Federal Project Officer, Grant Officer, or other authorized Awarding agency representative because of an audit or monitoring finding:

(a) Which resulted from a violation or possible violation of a statute, regulation, or the terms and conditions of a Federal award, including for funds used to match Federal funds;

(b) Where the costs, at the time of the audit, are not supported by adequate documentation; or

(c) Where the costs incurred appear unreasonable and do not reflect the actions a prudent person would take in the circumstances.

(d) Questioned costs are not an improper payment until reviewed and confirmed to be improper as defined in Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-123, Appendix C (see also the definition of improper payment in [2 CFR 200.1](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.1)).

271\. Revise subparts B and C to read as follows:

( printed page 32292)


# Subpart B—General Provisions

[§ 2900.4](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2900.4)

Adoption of [2 CFR part 200](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200).

The Department of Labor adopts the OMB regulation “Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards to Non-Federal Entities” (subparts A through F of [2 CFR part 200](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200)), as supplemented by this part, as Department of Labor policies and procedures for financial assistance administration. This part gives regulatory effect to the OMB regulation for Federal awards issued by the Department of Labor (DOL). The DOL also has programmatic and administrative regulations located in titles 20 and 29 of the CFR. See [2 CFR 200.110(a)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.110#p-200.110(a)) regarding the process for amending [2 CFR part 200](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200).

# Subpart C—Pre-Federal Award Requirements and Contents of Federal Awards

[§ 2900.5](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2900.5)

Federal awarding agency review of risk posed by applicants.

In addition to the regulation set forth in [2 CFR 200.206(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.206#p-200.206(b)), in evaluating risks of applicants, DOL also considers audits and monitoring reports containing findings and issues of noncompliance or questioned costs, in addition to reports and findings from audits performed under subpart F of [2 CFR part 200](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200) or the reports and findings of any other available audits (see [2 CFR 200.206(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.206#p-200.206(b))).

272\. Revise §§ 2900.7 and 2900.8 to read as follows:

[§ 2900.7](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2900.7)

Federal payment.

In addition to the regulation set forth in [2 CFR 200.305(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.305#p-200.305(b)), for Federal awards from the Department of Labor, the non-Federal entity should liquidate existing advances before it requests additional advances.

[§ 2900.8](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2900.8)

Cost sharing or matching.

In addition to the regulation set forth in [2 CFR 200.306(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.306#p-200.306(b)), for Federal awards from the Department of Labor, the non-Federal entity accounts for funds used for cost sharing or match within their accounting systems as the funds are expended.

273\. Revise §§ 2900.10 and 2900.11 to read as follows:

[§ 2900.10](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2900.10)

Prior approval requests.

In addition to the regulation set forth in [2 CFR 200.308(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.308#p-200.308(c)), for Federal awards from the Department of Labor, the non-Federal entity must request prior approval actions at least 30 days prior to the effective date of the requested action (see [2 CFR 200.407](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.407)).

[§ 2900.11](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2900.11)

Revision of budget and program plans including extension of the period of performance.

In addition to the regulation set forth in [2 CFR 200.308(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.308#p-200.308(b)), for Federal awards from the Department of Labor, the non-Federal entity must request prior approval for an extension to the period of performance.

274\. Revise §§ 2900.13 through 2900.15 to read as follows:

[§ 2900.13](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2900.13)

Intangible property.

In addition to the regulation set forth in [2 CFR 200.315(d)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.315#p-200.315(d)), the Department of Labor requires intellectual property developed under a discretionary Federal award process to be in a format readily accessible and available for open licensing to the public. An open license allows subsequent users to copy, distribute, transmit and adapt the copyrighted work and requires such users to attribute the work in the manner specified by the recipient.

[§ 2900.14](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2900.14)

Financial reporting.

In addition to the regulation set forth in [2 CFR 200.328](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.328), for Federal awards from the Department of Labor, the DOL awarding agency will prescribe whether the report will be on a cash or an accrual basis. If the DOL awarding agency requires reporting on an accrual basis and the recipient's accounting system is not on the accrual basis, the recipient will not be required to convert its accounting system, but must develop and report such accrual information through best estimates based on an analysis of the documentation on hand.

[§ 2900.15](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2900.15)

Closeout.

In addition to the regulation set forth in [2 CFR 200.344(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.344#p-200.344(b)), for Federal awards from the Department of Labor, the non-Federal entity must liquidate all financial obligations and/or accrued expenditures incurred under the Federal award. For non-Federal entities reporting on an accrual basis and operating on an expenditure period, unless otherwise noted in the grant agreement or cooperative agreement, the only liquidation that can occur during closeout is the liquidation of accrued expenditures (NOT financial obligations) for goods and/or services received during the grant period.

275\. Revise § 2900.16 to read as follows:

[§ 2900.16](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2900.16)

Prior written approval (prior approval).

In addition to the regulation set forth in [2 CFR 200.407](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.407), for Federal awards from the Department of Labor, the non-Federal entity must request prior written approval which should include the timeframe or scope of the agreement and be submitted not less than 30 days before the requested action is to occur. Unless otherwise noted in the grant agreement or cooperative agreement, the Grant Officer is the only official with the authority to provide prior written approval (prior approval). Items included in the statement of work or budget as awarded does not constitute prior approval.

276\. Revise § 2900.18 to read as follows:

[§ 2900.18](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2900.18)

Contingency provisions.

In addition to the regulation set forth in [2 CFR 200.433(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.433#p-200.433(c)), for Federal awards from the Department of Labor, excepted citations include [2 CFR 200.334](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.334) (retention requirements) and 200.335 (requests for records transfers).

[§ 2998.10](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2998.10)

What does this part do?

This part adopts the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by this part, as the Department of Labor (DOL) policies and procedures for non-procurement debarment and suspension. This part gives regulatory effect to the OMB regulation for Federal awards issued by DOL as supplemented


( printed page 32293)

by this part. This part satisfies the requirements in section 3 of [Executive Order 12549](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12549), “Debarment and Suspension” ( [3 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-3), 1986 Comp., p. 189); [Executive Order 12689](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12689), “Debarment and Suspension” ( [3 CFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-3), 1989 Comp., p. 235); and section 2455 of the Federal Acquisition Streamlining Act of 1994, 103 ( [31 U.S.C. 6101 note](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/31/6101)).


[§ 2998.20](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2998.20)

Does this part apply to me?

This part and, through this part, pertinent portions of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) (see table 2 to [2 CFR 180.100(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.100#p-180.100(b))) apply to you if you are a—

(a) Participant or principal in a “covered transaction” (see subpart B of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) and the definition of “non-procurement transaction” at [2 CFR 180.970](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.970));

(b) Respondent in a Department of Labor suspension or debarment action;

(c) Department of Labor debarment or suspension official; or

(d) Department of Labor grants officer, agreements officer, or other official authorized to enter into any type of non-procurement transaction that is a covered transaction.

[§ 2998.30](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2998.30)

What policies and procedures must I follow?

(a) The Department of Labor's policies and procedures that you must follow are specified in:

(1) Each applicable section of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180); and

(2) The supplement to each section of the OMB regulation that is found in this part under the same section number. (The contracts that are covered transactions, for example, are specified by [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220) as supplemented by § 2998.220.)

(b) For any section of OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) that has no corresponding section in this part, the Department of Labor's policies and procedures are those in the OMB regulation.

# Subpart A—General

[§ 2998.137](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2998.137)

Who in DOL may grant an exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction?

Within the Department of Labor, the Secretary of Labor or designee has the authority to grant an exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction, as provided in the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.135](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.135). If any designated official grants an exception, the exception must be in writing and state the reason(s) for deviating from the Government-wide policy in [Executive Order 12549](https://www.federalregister.gov/executive-order/12549).

# Subpart B—Covered Transactions

[§ 2998.220](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2998.220)

What contracts and subcontracts, in addition to those listed in [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220), are covered transactions?

In addition to the contracts covered under [2 CFR 180.220(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220#p-180.220(b)), this part applies to any contract, regardless of tier, that is awarded by a contractor, subcontractor, supplier, consultant, or its agent or representative in any transaction, if the contract is to be funded or provided by the Department of Labor under a covered non-procurement transaction. This extends the coverage of the Department of Labor non-procurement suspension and debarment requirements to all lower tiers of subcontracts under covered non-procurement transactions, as permitted under the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.220(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220#p-180.220(c)) (see optional lower tier coverage in the figure in appendix A to 2 CFR part 180).

# Subpart C—Responsibilities of Participants Regarding Transactions

[§ 2998.332](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2998.332)

What requirements must I pass down to persons at lower tiers with whom I intend to do business?

You, as a participant, must include a term or condition in lower-tier transactions requiring lower-tier participants to comply with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), as supplemented by this subpart.

# Subpart D—Responsibilities of Federal Agency Officials Regarding Transactions

[§ 2998.437](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-2998.437)

What method do I use to communicate to a participant the requirements described in the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435)?

To communicate to a participant the requirements described in [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435), you must include a term or condition in the transaction that requires the participant's compliance with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180), and supplemented by subpart C of this part, and requires the participant to include a similar term or condition in lower-tier covered transactions.

This part and, through this part, pertinent portions of the OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) (see table 2 to [2 CFR 180.100(b)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.100#p-180.100(b))) apply to you if you are a—

[§ 3000.30](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-3000.30)

What policies and procedures must I follow?

For any section of OMB regulation in subparts A through I of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180) that has no corresponding section in this part, Department of Homeland Security policies and procedures are those in the OMB regulation.

# Subpart A—General

[§ 3000.137](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-3000.137)

Who in the Department of Homeland Security may grant an exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction?

Within the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), the Secretary of Homeland Security has delegated the authority to grant an exception to let an excluded person participate in a covered transaction to the Chief Financial Officer for each DHS component as provided in the OMB regulation at [2 CFR 180.135](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.135).

# Subpart B—Covered Transactions

[§ 3000.220](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-3000.220)

What contracts and subcontracts, in addition to those listed in [2 CFR 180.220](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.220), are covered transactions?

Department of Homeland Security extends coverage of nonprocurement suspension and debarment requirements beyond first-tier procurement contracts under a covered nonprocurement transaction.

# Subpart C—Responsibilities of Participants Regarding Transactions

[§ 3000.332](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-3000.332)

What methods must I use to pass requirements down to participants at lower tiers with whom I intend to do business?

You as a participant in a covered transaction must include a term or condition in any lower-tier covered transaction into which you enter, to require the participant of that transaction to—

(a) Comply with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180); and

(b) Include a similar term or condition in any covered transaction into which it enters at the next lower tier.

# Subpart D—Responsibilities of Department of Homeland Security Officials Regarding Transactions

[§ 3000.437](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/05/29/2026-10817/regulation-for-federal-financial-assistance#sectno-citation-3000.437)

What method do I use to communicate to a participant the requirements described in the Office of Management and Budget regulation at [2 CFR 180.435](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-180.435)?

You as a DHS component official must include a term or condition in each covered transaction into which you enter, to communicate to the participant the requirements to—

(a) Comply with subpart C of [2 CFR part 180](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-180); and

(b) Include a similar term or condition in any lower-tier covered transactions into which the participant enters.
